description: One entry per command this repository ships that a contributor, a CI job, or an agent can run. Generated by re-executing every command against a freshly staged copy of the full allowlisted tree -- never hand-authored. `establishes` and `doesNotEstablish` are derived from each command's own runtime output (or, for the two certificate-run checks, from that script's own header comment, extracted fresh every generation run) -- never restated from memory. Regenerate with `node scripts/public-export/generate-capabilities.mjs`; check for drift with the same command plus `--check`.
howToUse: Each entry's `command` is the exact string to run from the repository root.
`establishes` and `doesNotEstablish` must both be reported together if you relay a result to anyone -- reporting only `establishes` overstates what the command showed.

`layer` names the earliest release layer (see export-manifest.json's own `layer` field, and README.md's 'How this repository is released') that stages the files this command needs. Compare it against the export-manifest.json in the checkout you are holding: if that manifest's `layer` is earlier in v0.1 < v0.2 < v0.3 < v0.4 order than this entry's `layer` (or the manifest's `layer` is null, meaning a full export), the command's files are not staged in this checkout and it will fail to find them -- that is expected, not a bug.

`offline` means the command needs nothing but a bare `node` already on PATH -- no install, no network, no build step. `requiresNetwork` means the command needs `pnpm install` (or equivalent) to reach a package registry first.
`runtimeMs` is a single measured sample from one generation run on one machine, not a guaranteed bound -- treat it as an order-of-magnitude expectation, not an SLA.

commands.summary: Confirms a certificate run's baked program VKey, statement digest and public-values digest really belong to the proof instance it is paired with, and that pairing the same run with a different instance is rejected.
establishes: twelve inputs, twelve stage records, every one VM-accepted
EVERY input's locking is P2SH32 of the redeem script carried in its own unlocking, and each body's length equals the reported `redeemBytes`

the gate redeem script bakes exactly five 32-byte constants, and numbers two, three and four are the instance's wrapper-key digest, public-values digest and PROGRAM VKEY — read out of the script, not out of the label
the fifth baked constant is the little-endian masked SHA-256 of the instance's public values (the gate's `statementDigest`)
input 1's unlocking carries that same scalar at offset 2, which is the binding the gate actually enforces at spend time
`provenance.instance.programVkeyHash` equals the program VKey found in the script, and equals `--expect-vkey` when one is given
`provenance.lockingGraphHash` recomputes from the emitted lockings
doesNotEstablish: The per-pair checks above are a MIXUP DETECTOR, not a forgery detector. They do not re-execute the CashVM transcript: `stageSummary[].accepted` is a REPORTED field that is read, never re-run. A determined party can therefore take the V1-keyed run, substitute the four keying constants in the gate, re-derive input 0's P2SH32 locking, patch input 1's limb, recompute `lockingGraphHash` and rewrite the identity block, and the per-pair checks will pass — because the eleven ARITHMETIC bodies are never looked at. That forgery was constructed and demonstrated during review of task 9.2.

The two cross-run checks below are what close that class, and they are the reason a run cannot be a relabelled copy of another: --distinct-bodies all twelve stage bodies must differ between the two runs. A relabelled copy shares them. --distinct-profile-identity the runtime-generic topology deriver, run on both runs under ONE fixed public-values template, must yield different profile identities. That deriver reviews and re-emits every arithmetic body, so its output moves only if the ladder really did. Both fail closed: if the deriver module cannot be loaded, that is a FAILURE and not a skip.

TASK 9.3 UPDATE — the consumption-time gap this file could not close is now closed inside the derivers themselves. `assertAPNTQuotientResidueCertificateRunIsKeyedToProgramVkeyV1` reads the baked program key out of a run's own gate redeem script and REFUSES to emit a topology for a different deployment. Everything below is unchanged; the `--distinct-profile-identity` fingerprint now opts out of that one check explicitly, because comparing two differently-keyed runs under one deriver is its entire purpose.

NOTE on `--distinct-profile-identity`: the deriver is the V1 runtime-generic one, and it is used here ONLY as a body-sensitive fingerprint under a fixed template. The value it returns for a V4-keyed run is NOT that run's V4 verifier profile identity — deriving that is task 9.3, and nothing here claims a V4 topology exists.
